items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I got some calls from Herbie Irving Mann and a whole lot of people, different ones, but they had to get permission from in order to use me

ctx.x: And I was ... like I say, I was kind of established now, recording with everybody during this period, and one day Philly Joe Billy Joe grabbed me one day and said, "Man, come over here to the Blue Note, and make this date with Lee Morlin and Horace Silver and Billy and myself -- it was Lee's first date day, I believe, doin' it, and we did -- called Lee Morlin, and I was fearful because I'm thinking of all this music that Lee got -- and he said, "Man, there ain't nothing to that," and I said, "Yeah, man, come on,"…

But they were teaching me like I never studied. But we got through that beautifully, and Alfred Lyon was very enthused -- he started calling me on quite a few record dates, and I got some calls from Herbie Irving Mann and a whole lot of people, different ones, but they had to get permission from in order to use me, and they signed me up with some options. Oh, but that was part of that New York scene.

Things kind of slowed up, and I worked a couple of gigs down at the Fire Spot Fireside and Dave Amram Amarand had a weekend down there with me, and I was in the rhythm section, and it was just a little hamburger joint on the Bowery there; we were
